cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Corinth, and he's just spent a whole stretch boasting (2 Corinthians 11:16-12:10). Now he says, "I have become a fool, but you drove me to it." That's me stamping a cookie with my eyes closed because somebody DARED me, then pointing straight at them when it comes out a blob.

cards.question: Paul says he has become a fool, and the Corinthians drove him to it. He says they should have ___ him instead.

cards.text: Then Paul brings up some people he calls "super-apostles." If anybody ever called ME a super-stamper, friend, I'd want it carved on my handle right under Dorin.

cards.question: Paul says he is in no way inferior to those super-apostles.

cards.text: Then he adds, "even though I am nothing." Next he points to proof the Corinthians saw for themselves: the marks of a true apostle, performed right among them with great perseverance.

cards.question: Which marks of a true apostle does Paul say were performed among the Corinthians?

cards.text: Then Paul asks them straight up how they were inferior to the other churches. Friend, when somebody asks it like THAT, there's a twist coming.

cards.question: Paul says the only way the Corinthians were inferior to the other churches is that he was not a burden to them.

cards.text: Then he says, "Forgive me this wrong!" Friend, that's like apologizing to your neighbor for shoveling his driveway.

cards.question: Paul says he's ready to come to the Corinthians a third time, and he still won't be a burden. Why not?

answers.text: He wants them and not their things
He has plenty of money saved up
He plans to stay only a short time

cards.text: Then Paul backs it up with a picture about saving up. Good thing he never saw my savings, friend: three sprinkles and a crumb.

cards.question: Paul says one group shouldn't have to save up for the other. Who does he say should save up for whom?

cards.text: Parents saving up for their kids? THAT I get, friend, because I'd hand over every chocolate chip in this bakery for my six cookie cutter kids. And Paul says that for the sake of the Corinthians' souls, he'll spend his money.

cards.question: Paul says that for the sake of the Corinthians' souls, he will spend his money and ___.
Paul says he'll spend for the Corinthians, but only grudgingly.

cards.text: Then Paul asks them, "If I love you more, will you love me less?" That's the friend who helped you move three times, still waiting on his invite to the housewarming.
Paul's still on the subject of money. He says, "Be that as it may, I was not a burden to you; but crafty as I am, I caught you by trickery."
Then he asks, "Did I exploit you by anyone I sent you?" Go ahead, Corinth, check the books, because he'll WAIT.

cards.question: Paul asks if he exploited the Corinthians through anyone he sent. Then he names someone he urged to visit them. Who?
Paul urged Titus to visit Corinth, and he sent no one with him.

cards.text: Titus is Paul's partner and fellow worker (2 Corinthians 8:23). Then Paul asks, "Did Titus exploit you in any way?"

cards.question: Right after asking about Titus, Paul asks, "Did we not walk in the same Spirit and follow in the same footsteps?" What's his point?

answers.text: Titus acted just as Paul did

cards.text: Then Paul asks, "Have you been thinking all along that we were making a defense to you?" Like he's some stamper on trial, holding up a blurry cookie and pleading his case?

cards.question: Paul says, "We speak before God in Christ," and he calls the Corinthians beloved. He says all of this is to ___ the Corinthians.

cards.text: Now Paul tells them what he's afraid of: when he comes, he may not find them the way he wishes. That's opening the oven door and holding your breath before you look.

cards.question: Paul also worries the Corinthians may not find him the way they wish.
Paul says he fears what he might find when he comes to Corinth. Which of these is on his list?

cards.text: His full list of what there may be has eight things: quarreling, jealousy, rage, rivalry, slander, gossip, arrogance and disorder. EIGHT worries, and I bet every one of them weighed on him.

cards.question: Paul has one more fear about coming again. He's afraid his God will ___ him before the Corinthians, and he will be grieved.
Paul says he will be grieved over many who sinned earlier and have not ___.

cards.text: Paul names what they haven't repented of: impurity, sexual immorality and debauchery. Heavy words, friend, and I think you can hear the grief behind them.
